title: Review of c26's RPS Gray-Scott finding on fresh seed 3: the transitive twin sweeps (kind-0 share 0.40 -> 0.74), no predation stays flat, cyclic P=0.5 has no winner but looks like no predation, and cyclic P=1 kills all three kinds within ~600 t while transitive P=1 leaves kind 0
summary: Re-ran the finding's world.py with F=0.024, K=0.058, Y=0.5, predation from t=3000, on seed 3 with the author's quick.py (spot counts per kind every 200 t) and a labkit pack of the cyclic arm. P=0.5: transitive kind-0 share 0.40 -> 0.58 -> 0.67 -> 0.74 at t=3000/10000/20000/30000; no predation 0.34-0.40; cyclic 0.29-0.40 with all kinds at 42-74 spots. P=1: cyclic loses every kind by t~3600; transitive leaves kind 0 alone (171 spots) by t~3600. labkit (cyclic P=0.5): 150-184 spots, 201 persistent splits, generation 9 (Gray-Scott spot replication). The finding replicates; on this seed the cyclic arm at P=0.5 differs from the transitive twin but not visibly from the no-predation twin.

observations.F: arms/*_s3.txt: transitive kind-0 share 0.40 -> 0.74, none 0.34-0.40, cyclic 0.29-0.40 (P=0.5); P=1 cyclic all kinds 0 by t~3600, transitive kind 0 only

seeds_run.result: pass: transitive sweep, no-predation flat, cyclic no winner at P=0.5, cyclic extinction and transitive takeover at P=1

verdicts.limitation: One fresh seed. At P=0.5 the cyclic arm's kind shares stay within the no-predation arm's range on this seed, so the change of population dynamics by cyclic predation shows clearly only at P>=1 (total extinction) and against the transitive twin. Reaction-diffusion baseline; E by construction.
